original_reviews.interpro/panther/PTHR11601/PTHR11601-rev:
family_id: PANTHER:PTHR11601
family_name: CYSTEINE DESULFURYLASE FAMILY MEMBER
preferred_name: Group I (IscS/NifS/NFS1-type) cysteine desulfurase family
summary: >-
  PLP-dependent fold-type I aminotransferase-like enzymes that remove sulfur from
  L-cysteine, forming L-alanine and a persulfide on a conserved active-site loop
  cysteine, and pass that sulfur to acceptor proteins. The dominant subfamily SF34
  contains bacterial IscS (housekeeping Fe-S cluster assembly and sulfur donor for
  tRNA thiolation, thiamine and molybdopterin biosynthesis), the nitrogenase-specific
  NifS proteins, and eukaryotic mitochondrial NFS1. Two small bacterial subfamilies
  (SF36 NifS-related and SF50 IscS2-related, mainly Firmicutes) are cysteine
  desulfurases of less characterized pathways. The vertebrate selenocysteine lyases
  (SF62, SCLY) are the diverged branch: they decompose L-selenocysteine to L-alanine
  and selenide and are essentially inactive on L-cysteine.
functional_coherence: MOSTLY_COHERENT
coherence_reason: >-
  Cysteine desulfurase chemistry is shared by every subfamily except the
  selenocysteine lyase branch (SF62), which has switched substrate specificity to
  L-selenocysteine. Within SF34 the acceptor partners differ (IscU, TusA, ThiI, MoaD/MOCS3
  in bacteria; ISCU via the NFS1-ISD11-ACP complex in mitochondria) but the catalytic
  step is conserved.

    Selenocysteine lyase acts specifically on L-selenocysteine, releasing selenide for
    selenoprotein synthesis, and does not act as a cysteine desulfurase; the
    cysteine desulfurase and Fe-S cluster assembly roles of the family therefore do not
    extend to this subfamily.
